findings.desc: M6 parity report does not exercise the actual optimized runtime path. CHK-004 promises reference full-scan, indexed runtime, and cached runtime gold queries, but runPlaybookRuntimeOptimizedParityReport reads records.jsonl and calls local report helpers instead: runIndexedColdScan still iterates every raw record and computes a local shortlist (packages/main/src/core/playbook-runtime-baseline.ts:1119), while runIndexedWarmCache only returns a digest from a new one-entry Map (packages/main/src/core/playbook-runtime-baseline.ts:1150). That path never drives buildMemoryFreshnessPack through RuntimeMemoryIndex/selectRuntimeMemoryIndexCandidates or the M3 cache get/remember boundary (packages/main/src/core/playbook-runtime-memory.ts:623, packages/main/src/core/playbook-runtime-memory-cache.ts:336, packages/main/src/core/playbook-runtime-memory-cache.ts:381), so the actual M3/M4 consumer index/cache could regress while the million parity report stays green. The M6 evidence should either run the real optimized runtime pack/cache path at the million-record boundary or downgrade the claim so it is not used as proof of indexed/cached runtime parity.
